how_to:
Understand The Purpose

The purpose of this journal is to help you keep your connection with your 'homeland' whilst you are doing your duties as an ambassador here on earth. Remember that you are not a spirit looking for a supernatural experience, but you are a spirit that is having a natural experience. Supernatural is supposed to be a norm to you.

About The Dates

Whilst there is nothing wrong in following the dates of the calendar, this journal has been designed to free you from the dates, thus allowing you to have control over the dates as you make entries herein. It is provided in good faith that you will be true to your devotion to the Lord whom you owe it all to.

Document Your Prayer Items

Writing down your prayer items helps you to keep track of the petitions that you have made to the Father. It will help you tick it off when you have received the answer to any of the items. Going back over the items will serve as a reminder in aligning your everyday language to your prayer items and scripture.

Scriptural References

The references to scripture are there to give you a nudge in the right direction. You need to make it your sworn responsibility to search the scriptures, and thus making the study of the Word of God your second nature. That is how you will thrive and be victorious in the spiritual environment.

Take Time To Meditate

Much of the answers to prayer come during the time taken to meditate on the Word of God. That is the time when God has the chance to direct and lead you in the paths of righteousness. Give God the time that He needs to put out words that you so desperately need in your spirit to change situations and circumstances in your life and in the world. Write down what He tells you in the journal; that way you will never forget it, and you will keep meditating on those words.

Engaging In Active Expectation

You receive what you expect to receive. Learn the art of expecting from the pregnant woman. She takes the time to focus on what she is expecting, talks about it as though it is already there, nurtures it, prepares and makes room for it until it manifests as her bundle of joy. That is how to expect and to receive from God – by aligning your words and actions to your expectation.

An Attitude Of Gratitude

Giving thanks to the Father of lights everyday keeps your faith sharp and engaged at all times. You acknowledge that the answer to your prayer has already been granted even when you do not yet see the manifestation in the natural. It puts you in a place where, like your Father God, you call things that be not as though they were (Romans 4:17).

This prayer journal will not only change your prayer life, but it is meant to impact and change your entire spiritual life and relationship with the Godhead for the better, and for good.

introduction:
As you engage through this prayer journal, I would like to encourage you to see this not as just another religious exercise, but as an engagement with God. You must change your attitude towards prayer and have a clear understanding of what prayer is about. Proverbs 24:3-4 reads, “Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established: and by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.” Amongst other meanings embedded in this scripture passage, your engagement with God in prayer is clearly laid out. Prayer is a very exciting way of communicating with God. It is in prayer that you realise the reality of God and His yearning to engage with you on a daily basis. That is what Adam used to enjoy in the cool of the day before the fall (Genesis 3:8). Prayer should never take the definition of an errand or chore; it is fellowship or communion with God. It is where you discover your purpose – the reason for being. And when you do you will find out that there is nothing on earth more exciting than walking with God.

Understanding what prayer is about establishes your prayer life. It is here that you understand that a prayer life goes beyond thirty minutes, or forty-five minutes, or an hour on your knees. You will understand that prayer goes far beyond asking for this or that from God, but it is your lifestyle wherever you are. You will understand that your speech will be the same when you are talking to God as when you are speaking with a fellow human being. You will understand that what God does to you in your secret place of prayer will be seen out in the public space. That was what defined the ministry of our Lord Jesus.

What Happens In The Prayer Closet

There are amazing things that happen when you are with God in the secret place. This is what most believers miss. They rush in and out of the prayer room, and in the process come out with nothing. You cannot go in the presence of a loving and giving God and come out emptyhanded.

  • In prayer, Joseph came out with a kingdom;
  • in prayer, Hannah came out with a prophet and judge of Israel;
  • in prayer, David came out with a kingdom;
  • in prayer, Esther came out with deliverance for Israel;
  • in prayer, Mary came out with a Saviour of mankind.

What will you come out with from your prayer closet?

I want to challenge you to approach prayer with a completely different attitude. This subject is so broad that we cannot explore it fully in this platform because it encompasses all of you – who you are, what you do, what you become, and all other aspects of your life. This is where dreams are conceived, nurtured and delivered. This is the place from where you carry the blessing of the Lord and deliver it to humanity. This is where no room for selfishness exists – you learn that your life is not your own, but a vehicle through which you become a blessing to all of humanity. Every man or woman that has ever lived a life of true prayer has walked out of the closet to become a great blessing to the people of God in one way or another. It is not for the privileged few, but for all of us. It just depends on how you respond to the call to prayer and what you do with what is given to you.

An effective prayer life will fill you with all precious and pleasant riches. This is the kind of prayer that is based on the word of God, and that empowers the believer to be a partaker of the divine nature (2 Peter 1:4). Prayer is central to us partaking of God's nature. It develops you to approach life and all its intricacies with God's attitude, devoid of fear and worry, but full of resting in the promises of God. Worry becomes foreign to a man or woman who knows how to connect with God in prayer.

“If my people, who are called by My name, will humble themselves and pray and seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sins and will heal their land” (2 Chronicles 7:14, NIV)

secrets.title: Do Away With Religion
secrets.teaching:
If prayer is going to be a lifestyle for you, then you will need to seriously consider doing away with religion and religious traditions. This is not rhetoric; it is serious enough for even the Lord Jesus to think of mentioning it when He taught His disciples about prayer in Matthew 6:5,7 (AMP), “Also when you pray, you must not be like the hypocrites, for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by people. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full already… And when you pray, do not heap up phrases (multiply words, repeating the same ones over and over) as the Gentiles do, for they think they will be heard for their much speaking.”

Needless to mention, if Jesus thought it necessary to point that out, then it means that it is something people normally get caught up in, thinking that they are doing the right thing, when in fact they are not. This means that most of the things that we usually think we know about prayer are really useless religious practices. No wonder many people have the idea that God takes long to answer prayer. That has never been the case in any normal conversation even among human beings; why then should it be normal when it comes to God? Study your Bible closely, and you will find that God answers prayer just as normally as any people would talk to each other. What brought about these ideas about God taking long to answer prayer? It is because people approach prayer with a religious attitude and without the knowledge of who God is and how He operates. Also, they have listened to people teaching them about a subject of prayer that they themselves know nothing about. And so now, like the disciples of the Lord Jesus, humble yourself to receive instruction in prayer, and pay attention to what the Word – not religion – says about it. The ideal about prayer is that the interaction of your petition and answer should happen in real time. That is the biblical presentation of the subject when God's people interact with Him. Study the following scripture passages: Genesis 3:8-13; 7:1-5; 12:1-4; 15:1-6; 18:22-33; 32:24-29; Exodus 3:1-22; 4:1-27; 1 Samuel 3:3-4, 9-15; 30:1-19; 2 Samuel 5:17-25; 1 Kings 3:5-15, 28; 17:1-5; 2 Chronicles 20:1-20; Isaiah 6:8-12; 38:1-6; 59:1-3; Jeremiah 1:4-15; Ezekiel 37:3-14; Daniel 10:2-14; Habakkuk 2:1-4; Luke 1:11-20, 28-38; Acts 4:23-31; 9:3-6, 10-18; 10:1-21; 13:2-3.

You are now not permitted to proceed reading until you have taken time through all the scriptures listed heretofore. These scripture passages are a picture of how the Lord operates – His modus operandi – when it comes to interacting with man.

Now let the Word debunk and set you free from that religious thought that will now creep into your mind and whisper, “But these were special servants of God who walked with Him in a special way, and that is why it is recorded in the Bible.” That is a lie from the pit of hell and it is meant to keep you bound in religion. James 5:17-18 (NIV) says, “Elijah was a human being, even as we are. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years. Again he prayed, and the heavens gave rain, and the earth produced its crops.” The scriptures quoted above are meant to unlearn you of all the religious programming that was engrained in your thinking about prayer or fellowship with the LORD. He has not changed, and He will never change (Malachi 3:6; James 1:17). We are the ones that must cast out our religious inclinations and adjust to His way of thinking and doing. Approach this exercise like a little child that is eager to learn new things, and with childlike faith embrace the instruction of the Lord prescribed in this journal. “And he said, Truly I tell you, unless you change and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven” (Matthew 18:3, NIV).

devotions.title: First Things First
devotions.html: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.” The Word is the law that governs the realm of the spirit. You are likely to lose a case if you go to court without the knowledge and understanding of the law that applies to the case. The same is true for spiritual things. Strive to be a passionate student of the word of God (the Bible in its entirety). God's people are destroyed because of the lack of knowledge of the word of God (Hosea 4:6). You limit the effectiveness of your prayer life if you embark on it without a commitment to the word of God.

devotions.title: Confess Your Sins
devotions.html: Keep sin confessed out of your life. No, this is not a consciousness; it is meant to keep communication channels uninterrupted between you and God. The word guides us to pray along these lines: “Father, due to my imperfection, if I have in any way sinned against You by commission or omission in thought, word or deed, I repent and plead the blood of Jesus to cleanse me of the unrighteousness, in Jesus' name.” This helps you to be ever conscious of the holiness of the God that you are interacting with. (See Daniel 9:1-19).

devotions.title: Confess Your Sins (Part 2)
devotions.html: Be reminded that you do not confess your sins because you are a sinner, but because you are progressively growing into the image of Christ. You may stumble and miss it in the process, and therefore you do not need to be held back by any sin, known or unknown. Repentance is a norm in the process of growth. The mere fact that you are still growing indicates that you are not perfect, and you need to understand and acknowledge that. In that manner, the enemy shall have no foothold on you or drag you over in the area of doubt and condemnation (Romans 8:1).

devotions.title: No Longer A Sinner
devotions.html: The phrase “while we were still sinners” in Romans 5:8 implies that you are no longer a sinner. 1 John 3:1 (NIV), “See what great love the Father has lavished on us, that we should be called children of God.” Religion will insist on you labeling yourself a sinner, but that is an insult to the grace of God and the work of the Cross. Your title is no longer 'sinner' but 'child of God'. You cannot be both at the same time. Get rid of that sinner identity once and for all. “We know that God does not listen to sinners. He listens to the godly person who does His will” (John 9:31, NIV).

devotions.title: Seated With Christ
devotions.html: “And He raised us up together with Him and made us sit down together [giving us joint seating with Him] in the heavenly sphere [by virtue of our being] in Christ Jesus (the Messiah, the Anointed One)” (AMP). A sinner cannot be made to sit with Christ in heavenly places. You are a new creature in Christ Jesus. Approach the presence of God with the confidence that He has made you His righteousness – one that can stand before Him without a sense of guilt or condemnation. Come boldly into the throne room of grace (Hebrews 4:16).

devotions.title: In His Image
devotions.html: Even though you cannot see God with your eyes, you ought not really struggle to figure out God's form. Scripture describes Him in several places. The point is that you are made in His image (Psalm 139:13). But how? Your body is nothing more than the clothing for your spirit the same way that your outfit is clothing for your body. You were not made to fit into your clothes, but your clothes were made to fit you. That is how your body is in relation to your spirit. Your mouth, hands and feet are an extension of God's mouth, hands and feet. Jesus said that the Father has a human form (John 14:9; Hebrews 1:3).

devotions.title: In His Image (Part 2)
devotions.html: God is described as a consuming fire (Hebrews 12:29). But the prophet Ezekiel gives a more striking description of Him when he said, “I saw that from what appeared to be His waist up He looked like glowing metal, as if full of fire, and that from there down He looked like fire; and brilliant light surrounded Him” (Ezekiel 1:27, NIV). When you develop yourself in the spirit through constant fellowship with Him in prayer and the Word you get to the point where you look like that also because you are made in His image.

devotions.title: God Is For You
devotions.html: Understand that God is for you (on your side) and not against you. He wants to work on your behalf more than you can ever imagine. He is more eager to be with you than you are to be with Him. He has chosen to love you when you least deserved it; how much more now that you are His child and a member of His own household? Romans 5:8 (NIV) says, “But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” Do not fear to draw near to Him; He has been expecting you to do so for a long time.

devotions.title: In God’s Class
devotions.html: As you walk into your prayer closet, realise that you approach a Person that has accepted you in His class (Hebrews 4:15-16). You do not approach Him unworthily; He decided to make you worthy, not by your own righteousness, but through the blood of Jesus Christ. You have every right to fall on His lap as a well-beloved child. Ephesians 5:1 (AMP), “Therefore be imitators of God [copy Him and follow His example], as well-beloved children imitate their father].” You cannot imitate something in whose class you do not belong. You belong in God's class.

devotions.title: Fellowship With God
devotions.html: You fellowship with God because you have a relationship with Him. He is your Father, and you are His child. Graduate from going to God on the basis of needs and learn to spend time with Him because you enjoy His presence. Learn to not spend time with God only in time of a crisis, be it healing or financial breakthrough or when in need of the non-essential stuff that some have made a priority in their lives. Just have a 'You and me' time with God, sometimes without having to ask anything from Him: He enjoys that a lot (John 15:14-15). It will not be long before His reality to you gets stronger and stronger.

devotions.title: Not By Sight
devotions.html: It does not matter that you do not see God with your physical eyes; that is irrelevant. He is more real than the floor that you kneel on or anything else that you can see. He is not some 'invisible influence'; He is a Person that cannot be seen because He is a Spirit, which is why we are called to worship Him in spirit and in truth (John 4:24). The only difference between you and Him is that you have a physical body and He does not. Do not let your body hinder your fellowship with Him; He is not bothered by that, and neither should you. In prayer you should allow a spirit to spirit communion to take place between you and God.

devotions.title: Love His Word
devotions.html: “Do not forsake wisdom, and she will protect you. Love her, and she will watch over you” (Proverbs 4:6, NIV). When you love someone, you just cannot help but want to spend time with them. Jesus demonstrated His love for you by dying for you on the cross. You demonstrate your love for Him by desiring and striving to become like Him. You are predestined to be molded into the image of Jesus so that you will look alike with Him as your Big Brother, and you His little brother or sister (read Romans 8:29 and Hebrews 2:11-12).

devotions.title: God Speaks
devotions.html: The Bible is God's word speaking to you. One of the best ways to enjoy your walk with God is by learning to hear God when He speaks to you. But you will have to get very acquainted with the written word of God first. God speaks just as well as, and even better than you do. The reason people struggle to hear Him speak is because they do not know His voice. Jesus said, “I have other sheep that are not of this sheepfold. I must bring them also. They too will listen to (or hear) my voice, and there shall be one flock and one shepherd” (John 10:16, NIV). The voice is used for speaking, and is meant to be heard.

devotions.title: God Speaks (Part 2)
devotions.html: The reason you have to learn to hear the voice of God is because speaking and hearing are two elements of the communication process. Religion teaches that when you pray, God will hear and answer when He wants to. That is the impression given which makes prayer boring when you seem to be speaking to a stone that does not answer. That is not the God described in the Bible. The God of the Bible hears and speaks back when His children engage with Him in prayer. The Word of God will train you to recognise the voice of God when He speaks because He speaks directly to your spirit and not your physical ears. Feed your spirit with God's word like you feed your body with food.

devotions.title: Learn To Listen
devotions.html: “My son, pay attention to what I say; turn your ear to my words” (NIV). That is God's invitation to you. Notice that it is your decision to listen to God. He will speak to and be heard by anyone who deliberately listens. Many times you can hear the voice of your body when it says “I'm hungry; …I'm sick; …I'm tired.” You can hear the voice of fear when it says “You will never make it this time; …you will not recover from this disease.” All those are voices speaking to you and you hear them because you are used to them through your body and circumstances. Well, God's voice is also active, but you need to tune in to the right frequency to hear it.

devotions.title: Learn To Listen (Part 2)
devotions.html: Your lifespan is a long and boring one if you cannot hear the voice of the God that you claim to follow. It is never meant to be that way. Anybody can turn their ear to the voice of God if they want to. It is not meant for the 'special' selected few; it is for whoever will do what it takes to hear it. Hearing the voice of God is what will help you lead a meaningful and fulfilling life here on earth. It is then that you will be able to step into God's paths for your life so that you can be a blessing to all of humanity (Psalm 23:3). “When you walk, they will guide you; when you sleep, they will watch over you; when you awake, they will speak to you” (Proverbs 6:22).

devotions.title: The Principal Thing
devotions.html: “Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding.” The wisdom of God is the Word of God. We know that Christ has been made unto us the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:30; John 1:1-4, 14). Therefore getting wisdom is getting the word of God. It is talking primarily about the written word of God, which we refer to as the Holy Bible. The first step to learning to hear the voice of God is by constantly studying His word (the Bible), and giving yourself completely to it.

devotions.title: The Principal Thing (Part 2)
devotions.html: The day that you will believe the report of the word of God (as written in the Bible) more than you believe what is written in the newspaper will be the day of your breakthrough as a child of God. You ought to be so bent by the word of God to where nothing that you see or feel can convince you against the report of the word of God. You only reach that point by continually studying your Bible. Your progress will become visible to everyone as you take a plunge in the Word and meditatively cling to it (1 Timothy 4:15).

devotions.title: God Your Rewarder
devotions.html: “And without faith it is impossible to please God, because anyone who comes to Him must believe that He exists and that He rewards those who earnestly seek Him” (NIV). When you come to God you must do so in faith, believing that He is interested in you and what you have to communicate to Him just like any father has his children's interest at heart. He is ever there and available for you, and the only reason you have to 'seek Him' is because of this veil of your physical body that makes it a challenge to relate with a Spirit being; yet He is just as real.

devotions.title: The Great Teacher
devotions.html: “But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth. He will not speak of his own; he will speak only what he hears, and he will tell you what is yet to come” (NIV). The Holy Spirit works together with the word of God to lead and guide you. Beloved, this leadership and guidance is real just like any man can guide you through unfamiliar territory. As much as you give yourself to the written Word of God, you should also seek to co-operate with the Holy Spirit that has been given to you. A child of God has no reason to fumble when the Holy Spirit is in his or her life. Get to know the Holy Spirit for your own good.

secrets.title: All Your Life Is Prayer
secrets.teaching:
You cannot separate your prayer life from your daily life, including all that which is entailed in your life. A separation of prayer and daily life activities is what results in most of the defeat and unanswered prayers in the lives of believers. The same faith applicable in prayer must be the same faith applicable in your life in general. That is what scripture means when it says that the just shall live by faith (Habakkuk 2:4; Hebrews 10:38). Pay attention to this: words govern all of reality, and that is how God designed life to operate. You cannot say one thing in the prayer closet, and then go on to say something else that is in contradiction to what you said in that prayer when you are outside the closet. It just will not work (Mark 11:23-24).

You have to get your life in order to the point that whatever you say in public or among friends, co-workers, relatives, and so on is in total agreement with what you said to God in prayer. You are still the same person in the prayer closet and outside the closet, and He is still the same God answering your prayer. So what does this mean? It means that if you base your prayer on the word of God, then you will also keep your lips from speaking guile (Psalm 34:13). Hypocrisy is when you speak one way before God, trying to convince Him that you are aligned with His word and you have faith, and then speak something in the contrary when you are not addressing Him. That is deceit. The person who does that must never think that he or she will receive anything from the Lord (James 1:6). Now you realise the reason to have yourself totally soaked in the word of God… living by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4).

Does that sound like being over the top? No, it is not being over the top; it is assuming what you should always be according to the plan of God for your life. What makes people fail to receive answers to their prayers? James teaches that it is praying on the basis of their lustful desires (James 4:1-3). Lustful desires are those desires that are not based on the word of God, for the word of God (or the promises embedded in it) causes us to escape the corruption that is in the world through lust (2 Peter 1:4). “How do I pray the word of God all the time? Is my life supposed to be the word of God?” Most definitely! That is what God has been after all along. You have to come to the point where you realise that your life and the answers to your prayers is not about you. The day you fully understand this truth and embrace it will be the turning point of fully experiencing the joy of answered prayers. Our problem is that we have been taught or made to believe in selfishness. We ask for all the things that address our selfish desires. The Lord Jesus spoke about this in Matthew 6:25-33. Please pause now and read that scripture passage and reflect on it and try to extract or draw personal lessons from it.

The paramount lesson that you must have learnt from Matthew 6:25-33 should be that none of the things that pertain to our mundane lives should be your concern, but that you should rather be concerned about the kingdom of God and becoming like Him. It is when you get to this point that all these things that you need for your earthly existence shall be added to you. No, this is not to say that you do not need all those things; it is to say rather that they are not primary. And besides, your heavenly Father knows that you have need of all those things (Matthew 6:32). But needing them does not mean that you should seek after them, for then are you not different from those who do not even know God. Therefore, if you seek the heart of God in prayer, He will be obliged by the promise He made in Matthew 6:33 to see to it that those things that you need for your earthly existence are catered for in excess of your expectations (Ephesians 3:20).

But how do you get to where you are concerned with the heart of God? It is by surrounding yourself with the word of God to where nothing matters to you more than the word of God. That is what is meant by Proverbs 4:5-9, which reads: “Get wisdom, get understanding; do not forget my words or turn away from them. Do not forsake wisdom, and she will protect you; love her, and she will watch over you. The beginning of wisdom is this: get wisdom. Though it cost all you have, get understanding. Cherish her, and she will exalt you; embrace her, and she will honour you. She will give you a garland to grace your head and present you with a glorious crown” (NIV).

devotions.title: Invite The Holy Spirit
devotions.html: Yours is a life in the spirit because you are a spirit being. Do not be pulled back or deceived by the physical aspect of your existence; do not be fooled by the house (or tabernacle) that you live in (1 Corinthians 6:19; 2 Peter 1:14). Therefore it is in your best interest that you develop a close relationship with your fellow spirit being called Holy Spirit. He is your best prayer partner who will teach you the best way to pray (Romans 8:26-27). He is in you right now, but He is such a gentle Spirit who will only be involved in your life when He is invited to do so. Learn to acknowledge Him at all times just like you acknowledge a friend who has visited you.

devotions.title: Entertain The Holy Spirit
devotions.html: The most painful thing you can do to a guest is to ignore them. We all know how to entertain our guests so that they feel welcome in our space. Holy Spirit is as much a guest as any other, and much better than the rest, and He does appreciate being entertained. Deliberately train your mind to remember His presence in your life all the time (Romans 8:14; Galatians 5:18,25). You need Him more than you need the oxygen that you breathe. He is the power that brings everything to pass in your life. He is the power that brought this entire universe into being (Genesis 1:2; Matthew 12:28), and He now dwells within you (John 14:17).

devotions.title: Engage The Holy Spirit
devotions.html: Learn to engage the Holy Spirit in your prayer life. That is one way in which you cultivate a consciousness of His presence all the time. Also, He will teach you how to pray as you allow the prayer language of the Spirit to take over as you pray. The prayer language of the Spirit is what we refer to as other tongues (1 Corinthians 14:14-15). That is the most powerful way of prayer as it closes out everybody else except God who is involved with your praying (1 Corinthians 14:2). Many believers still have a problem understanding this aspect of prayer, but it does not change what is written about it.

devotions.title: Your Prayer Assistant
devotions.html: “In the same way, the Spirit helps us in our weakness. We do not know what we ought to pray for, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us through wordless groans. And He who searches the hearts knows the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for God's people in accordance with the will of God” (NIV). A prayer life without engaging the Holy Spirit is like a bird trying to fly with one wing; it will be extremely limited. Many times you will not know what to pray for or even how to pray, but the Holy Spirit knows exactly how to do it in you.

devotions.title: Be God-inside Minded
devotions.html: Settle it in your mind that God is not out there, but He is in you, and has become one with you. Know that He is closer to you than the next person in your room when you relate with Him in prayer. And like Proverbs 18:24 says, He is a friend that is closer than a brother. Get rid of this 'God-in-heaven out there' mentality and understand that He dwells within you (Luke 17:20-21). If the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit have chosen to make their home within you, then why look elsewhere for His kingdom? (John 14:23).

devotions.title: Understanding Prayer
devotions.html: “And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord's people” (NIV). Notice that there are different kinds of prayers that you are encouraged to employ in your prayer life. It is important to know this. It is like using different keys to open different doors that lead into different chambers. Using the wrong key will lock you out of the room that you need to enter. A lack of knowledge in this regard will greatly hinder and limit your prayer life. Conduct an intense study into this subject so that you can have a profitable prayer life.

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers
devotions.html: Prayer of Consecration is like the one made by our Lord Jesus when He was in the Garden of Gethsemane before His crucifixion (Matthew 26:39). This is the only kind of prayer that characterised by the phrase “if it be Your will.” Here you relinquish your own will to the will of God about an issue. In the natural, Jesus wanted to withdraw from the cross, but He laid His will aside and gave way to the Father's will to be done. This is also the prayer that must dominate most of the believer's life (Matthew 6:10; Acts 20:22-24). You come to the point where you acknowledge that your life is not about you anymore.

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 2)
devotions.html: The Prayer of Faith: “Is any sick among you? Let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him” (James 5:14-15). This is based on the known will and provision made by the Lord for our health and any other promise that is documented in the Word of God (2 Peter 1:3-4). Here it is no longer a matter of “if”; we know that it is His will to see us healed and our every need provided for (Philippians 4:19).

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 3)
devotions.html: Prayer of Supplication is the one wherein requests or petitions are made to the Lord. There are different petitions that can be made regarding our lives and the lives of those around us. Consistent with the calling of God on your life, you can ask for anything that is required for you to fulfil that calling and it will be granted to you (John 16:23-24). It is important to understand that the short life here on earth is best lived to the glory of God, meaning that we should endeavour not to live for ourselves but for God. This is where the offering of your body to the Lord as a living sacrifice becomes a reality (Romans 12:1).

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 4)
devotions.html: Prayer of Intercession is one where you stand in the gap for other people. This is central to a believer's life, as it indicates your desire to see the will of God done on earth through the salvation of as many people as possible. Abraham, Moses, David, Samuel, Jesus, the early apostles, and others that went after the heart of God offered this kind of prayer on a regular basis (Ezekiel 22:30-31). God is always looking for somebody to stand in the gap on behalf of individuals, communities and nations, to pray for God's mercy and destruction to be averted, thereby giving them a chance to repent (1 Timothy 2:1-4).

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 5)
devotions.html: Prayer of Agreement is described by Jesus in Matthew 18:19, “Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of My Father which is in heaven.” This is the prayer of agreement that may be offered by friends, couples, or a body of believers in a corporate setting (Acts 4:23-31). The unrest and atrocities in our lands can be brought to a standstill if believers could understand the power in this kind of prayer, but we must be in total agreement to see the results. Anyone who cannot raise his faith level to the agreement should excuse himself from participating in this prayer.

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 6)
devotions.html: Prayer of Binding and Loosing will work in conjunction with the prayer of agreement, albeit not limited to that. One or more believers can, in faith, exercise their authority to bind or loose activities in the spirit (Matthew 18:18). The binding or loosing in heaven does not refer to where God dwells because there is nothing there that requires either of these. It refers to the demonic realm that controls the things that manifest in this world in different forms such as murders, injustice, violence, gangsterism and all sorts of evil (Psalm 149:6-9).

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 7)
devotions.html: Prayer of Praise and Thanksgiving should accompany all other kinds of prayers that we offer to God. “Do not be anxious about anything, but in every situation, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God” (Philippians 4:6, NIV). An attitude of gratitude at all times keeps your heart in a receiving mode concerning the things asked for. Thanksgiving and praise paralyses the enemy who would otherwise move in to hinder your receiving. “Through the praise of children and infants You have established a stronghold against your enemies, to silence the foe and the avenger” (Psalm 8:2, NIV).

devotions.title: Kinds Of Prayers (Part 8)
devotions.html: The Prayer of Communion is a powerful prayer that invests in your fellowship with God. It is beautiful to go before God just to spend time in fellowship with Him. This was and still is the reason God made man in the first place. Anybody will enjoy the company of a friend who will come to them not because they have a need, but because they value their relationship. “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother” (Proverbs 18:24). It is wonderful to take time to develop your friendship with God. Friendship lets you in on the entire heart of your friend (John 15:14-45; Isaiah 41:8; James 2:23).

devotions.title: Let Love Dominate
devotions.html: Nothing that concerns the Spirit of God will work outside of love. Love is the 'mechanism' that causes your faith to work. If you struggle with prayer that seems to go unanswered, the number one thing to check is your love walk. Love is best described in 1 Corinthians 13:4-8. That is the Love Checklist. To add on that, observing and living according to that checklist will make you more like God, for He is love. Those are the characteristics of God in a nutshell. It will do you good as a prayer warrior to spend time meditating on the rest of 1 Corinthians 13; it is your spiritual gateway without which nothing will work for you.

devotions.title: Synchronise Your Life
devotions.html: “Death and life are in the power of the tongue: and they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.” Let the words of your mouth work together with and be a reflection of what you believe in your heart. If you have trouble restraining your tongue, then you need to go back and lock yourself in with the word of God until it reprograms your heart and fills it with the Word, “for the mouth speaks what the heart is full of” (Matthew 12:34, NIV). It is easy to let your tongue loose and you speak death on situations around your life, but with discipline you can bring it in check through the word of God. You waste your time in prayer if you are not willing to do this.

devotions.title: Faith Versus Emotions
devotions.html: Beware of the trap of emotionalism when you go to God in prayer. There are believers who think that God answers their tears. Well, if He did, then most of the poor would be well-off by now because there is no telling to how many tears they have cried. Granted, situations can be painful, but it is faith, and not emotions, that will take us out of those situations. God, like any judge, is not moved by tears; He is moved by your faith. So you cannot manipulate God with tears when you have no faith, otherwise God will not be true to His word if He gives in to people's emotionalism. If crying works for you, then it had better be mixed with faith (Hebrews 11:6).

devotions.title: Watch Your Mouth
devotions.html: Strive to align your everyday speech with your prayer life. Do not pray for one thing, for example, the peace in your community, and then walk out of the prayer room and say, “You won't believe the division and wickedness in my neighbourhood!” You just cancelled your prayer! You just dug up the seed that you sowed, and how dare you expect it to germinate and yield a harvest? This is where many believers abort their prayers, by failing to keep a watch on their mouths. Proverbs 4:24 calls it a froward (false and dishonest) mouth and perverse lips, which you must learn to put away from you.

devotions.title: Speaking In Tongues
devotions.html: Note that there is a difference between praying in other tongues and speaking in other tongues. Failing to understand this creates confusion among believers. You can speak in tongues the whole day and wherever you may be, as long as you keep it within yourself (1 Corinthians 14:18-19). Speaking in tongues helps you to edify yourself in the spirit – it charges you up the same way you would charge your cellular phone battery (1 Corinthians 14:4). How do you edify yourself? You render your own spirit to become more sensitive to the Holy Spirit inside you. The more you speak in tongues the better for you and it can be done anytime, for example, when you are driving, doing house chores, or just walking.

devotions.title: Praying In Tongues
devotions.html: Praying in tongues helps you to address issues with God that may be difficult to articulate in your own language as you may not know how to do it (Romans 8:26-27). Sometimes you will not know what to pray for, but the Spirit helps you to address those issues. When you pray in the spirit you find yourself praying for things even in distant lands that you would never be aware of in any way. You can pray for people that are in trouble when you do not even know that is what you are doing. This happens as you follow the promptings of the Spirit to pray when you are in tune with the Holy Spirit as a result of constantly speaking in tongues.

devotions.title: A Life Of Worship
devotions.html: Worshiping God must not be limited to a church setting; it must be the lifestyle of the believer. Great things happen in the spirit and in the natural when believers learn to worship God in spirit and in truth. Notice that worship has nothing to do with how you feel. You do not do it because God has done something for you, but because He is worthy to be worshiped. Worship comes out of you not as a result of a command, but out of an appreciation of His goodness to you. If He has not done anything in your prayer list, He still deserves your worship because He has saved your soul from eternal damnation.

secrets.title: The Value Of Meditation
secrets.teaching:
“The rays of the Sun, diffused over the entire surface of the Earth, produce only a moderate warmth, but if even a few of them are concentrated by means of a glass, they are capable of producing fire at the focusing point. Thought force is the most powerful means of obtaining knowledge. If it is concentrated upon a subject, it will burn its way through any obstacle and solve the problem. If the requisite amount of thought is brought to bear, there is nothing that is beyond the power of human comprehension. So long as we scatter it, thought force is of little use to us, but as soon as we are prepared to take the trouble necessary to harness it, all knowledge is ours” ~ Max Heindel, The Rosicrucian Cosmo-conception (1909).

Thought force is a trait that all of humanity possesses, except that many practice it in the negative direction. The best way that I can explain this is by asking you a simple question: have you ever worried about anything in your life? Anyone who will say 'No' to this question is a liar because at one point or another we all have worried about something. Some of us worry about not worrying at all. So if you can worry, then you can meditate because worry is meditation on the lies of satan. All that you need to do is refocus your energy and meditate on what God has said to you, be it about who you are, or any of His promises to you, or whatever else proceeds from the mouth of God. That is how you are supposed to live: by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God (Deuteronomy 8:3; Matthew 4:4; Luke 4:4). These are the words that we need to learn to channel our thinking towards and expose our thought force to.

What is it that you are praying and believing God for? Is it healing, finances, peace in your life and home, protection for your children? Find a scripture that covers that area and go to God with it. Pray those two or three scripture verses to God in faith (2 Corinthians 13:1). Then sit back and soak your mind on those scriptures. 'Worry' those scriptures (so to speak), and mutter them to yourself long enough for them to start consuming your thought life. Once you reach that point you will notice your believing begin to change. Then what you see around you will not matter anymore instead of worry you will begin to speak the word based on the scriptures you are reading and meditating on. This will be a lifestyle whether you are speaking to yourself, to God, or to any other person around you.

Note that your biggest challenge is not that you do not believe. It is what you believe, which turns out to be what you speak, which then turns out to be the seed you sow, and ultimately the harvest that you reap. “I believed, therefore have I spoken” (Psalm 116:10; 2 Corinthians 4:13).

I must warn you though: meditation is not easy if you are not used to it, but it can be practiced by anybody. I would advise that you consider starting off learning to focus your mind on God's word for 10 or 15 minutes for a couple of days. Then you will graduate to maybe 25 to 30 minutes. And before you know it you'll be doing it for an hour or two. The goal is to get to the point of Joshua 1:8 (AMP), which says, “This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe and do according to all that is written in it…” This is one art that the devil stole from the church for ages; hence our churches and personal lives as believers have been so devoid of power. Meditation is where you develop your ability to hear God speak to you. Meditation burns the dirt off and unclogs the channel that should be open for you to communicate effectively with God. It works more like fine-tuning the channel so you can hear God clearly. However, you dare not venture into meditation if you do not constantly study the word of God because you will have to judge whatever you hear with the word of the living God.

devotions.title: The Lost Art
devotions.html: Meditation is an art that has been lost to the church for a long, long time. The reason is that the enemy knows the amount of power inherent in it. Also, thank God for the Western believers that took the gospel all over the world, but they know very little about meditation because the Bible, though it may be reproduced in the West, is not a Western book. The Bible says a lot about meditation. All its writers, inspired by the Holy Spirit, were Eastern people. Think about Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Joshua, and all the way to the apostles. All these knew the place of meditation in the life of a believer, and so should you.

devotions.title: Where To Start
devotions.html: Your biggest question at this point might be, “All good, but where do I start?” Start with easy to understand verses of scripture like “Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one Lord” (Deuteronomy 6:4). You can spend your whole prayer session, however long, thinking about this and whispering it to yourself. Fix your thoughts squarely on the statement, and establish in your thinking that you belong to and serve only one Lord. Then you shall know that “thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might” (Deuteronomy 6:5).

devotions.title: Delight In The Word
devotions.html: “But his delight is in the law of the Lord, and in His law doth he meditate day and night.” Prayer becomes not a chore but a delight when the child of God trains himself or herself to delight in the law of the Lord. You show your delight through meditating in that law (or Word) day and night. The Lord has not instituted prayer as a way of testing your obedience, but it a platform for a living fellowship with Him, which can be greatly enhanced through meditation. You cannot wait for your next prayer session when you know that it is a session of communion with God in stark reality.

devotions.title: Delight In The Word (Part 2)
devotions.html: God desires to speak to you “face to face, as one speaks to his friend” (Exodus 33:11). That was how God spoke to Moses in the Old Testament. We are in the New Testament that is “established upon better promises” (Hebrews 8:6). This means that if we let Him and position ourselves for it, the Lord has no problem speaking to us as one speaks to his friend. The question is: do we have faith to believe and expect it to be so? The Apostle John – Revelator – was that way because he chose His place in the bosom of the Lord (John 13:23-24). Jesus did not choose to love this man; he positioned himself for it, and so can we.

devotions.title: Word Of Warning
devotions.html: Whatever you do, see to it you are established on the firm foundation of the Word of God. If you practice meditation without being a staunch student of the Word you might open yourself up to deceiving spirits. Meditation will open up a whole new world into the spiritual, where there are many spirit beings, many of which might not be of God. Therefore you must train yourself to the voice of God through His word. Whatever you believe to have heard in the spirit, do not act upon it until you have judged it with the written Word of God by finding at least two or three scriptures that will back it up (Deuteronomy 19:15; Matthew 18:16; 2 Corinthians 13:1).

devotions.title: Word Of Warning (Part 2)
devotions.html: Going before God in prayer does not mean the enemy will not try to intrude and seek to mislead. If it happened to the Lord Jesus it will most likely happen to you too (Matthew 4:1-11; Hebrews 4:15). The devil barged into Jesus' prayer time in the wilderness and started quoting scriptures out of context. That was the same trick that he used on Eve in the Garden of Eden. Now if you do not know scripture properly you will take the bait just like Eve did. She was deceived, went on to drag her husband into it, and it cost them everything. There could have been a problem if Jesus did not know how to differentiate between the Father's voice and that of the devil.

devotions.title: Not An Easy Practice
devotions.html: Meditation is not an easy practice. Your mind is used to being scattered all over the place, and bringing it to focus on one subject will always be hard for the beginner, but it can be done through constant practice. Your mind will present 101 different things to think about when it is time to meditate. Do not give up; fix your mind on that one verse of scripture. An easier way to help your mind focus is to engage your mouth and speak that verse out. Your mind will always wait to hear what your mouth has to say. You cannot say one thing and think about another at the same time.

devotions.title: Thou Shalt Meditate
devotions.html: We read about how Bible characters used to walk with God in ways that is exemplary and desirable for today's believer. We miss a point about their habit that was endorsed by God because He instituted it, namely meditation. Today's believer has been taught to dismiss it as Eastern mysticism, but that is not what it is. It matters what you meditate upon. “Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all” (1 Timothy 4:15). Meditate upon what? Back up a little bit to find out – look at verses 13 and 14, and you will have an idea.

devotions.title: Meditation Versus Confession
devotions.html: Meditation is a function of the soul (where the mind is embedded) (Philippians 4:8), and confession is the function of the heart (Matthew 12:34). Therefore the two cannot be interchanged; they refer to two different activities. You speak what you have conveyed into your heart through meditation. If it is negative, it will be heard from your mouth; and if it is positive, your mouth will reveal it too. It is like this: if you take a lemon and squeeze it, never expect orange juice because it is not there. So when you are put under pressure, what is in your heart in abundance will come out of your mouth. Meditation will regulate these inevitable dynamics.

devotions.title: Follow The Example
devotions.html: “We do not want you to become lazy, but to imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised” (NIV). Abraham is one in whose steps we are admonished to follow (Romans 4:12; Isaiah 51:1-2). “And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide…” (Genesis 24:63). Where do you think Isaac learned the art of meditation? From his father Abraham, of course! “And the Lord appeared unto him in the plains of Mamre…” (Genesis 18:1). How do you think such appearances were triggered? Abraham was a man of deep meditation, and it always paid off.

devotions.title: Follow The Example (Part 2)
devotions.html: “Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in Thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer” (Psalm 19:14). Again you see from David's account how confession and meditation are two different activities. Meditation is a very important aspect of prayer. You miss out on so much when you pray and exclude meditation. Meditation is the act of fixing your thoughts on a particular subject of [spiritual] interest, thereby pushing away the rubble that covers valuable spiritual truths. Spiritually, it helps to extract the gold that is buried deep in the ground and bring it to the surface.

devotions.title: Power Of Meditation
devotions.html: “I meditate on Your precepts and consider Your ways” (NIV). The same way that worrying (or meditating about a problem) makes a problem more real and magnifies it in your thinking, so does meditating (or thinking deeply) on the word of God magnify the Lord and His promises in your thinking. You begin to see it as a reality and respond to it. If it is worry, then a confession based on fear will creep in, cripple and dominate you. If it is meditating on the goodness of God, then a blessed confession that brings faith will follow, leading to your victory. So, whether in the positive or negative, your life is built around meditation.

devotions.title: Power Of Meditation (Part 2)
devotions.html: Meditation opens up and burns your way through the iron curtain that keeps you from seeing and understanding life in its truest essence. “Be still and know that I am God” (Psalm 46:10). It is in the stillness of meditation that you get to know God more intimately. You move from knowing about God to actually knowing Him. Realities that are hidden from the eye of the flesh cannot escape the unrelenting gaze of meditation that burns through the crust of concealment and renders everything naked. “The path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day” (Proverbs 4:18).

devotions.title: Meditation And Confession
devotions.html: Even though meditation and confession are two different activities, they work best when they are paired together. “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night…” What causes the Word to not stop coming out of your mouth is your continuous meditation of it. The more you think about it is the more you will talk about it. And the more you talk about it is the more you participate in divine nature. It changes your prayer life, your reality and your world. It causes you to begin to think, talk and act like the Almighty God. He has built it in you to be that way; it is up to you to develop it.

devotions.title: Meditation And Guidance
devotions.html: “Blessed are those who listen to me, watching daily at my doors, waiting at my doorway” (NIV). Meditation opens your spiritual eyes to the realities of the unseen world where it becomes easier to see and hear in the spirit. It opens the spiritual ears to hear what the Spirit of God is saying to you as an individual, thereby taking you from the general to the specifics of God's word and plan or purpose about your own life. “Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches” (Revelation 3:6,13,22, NIV). “Whoever has ears, let them hear” (Matthew 13:9). These are not the physical ears or eyes, but the ears or eyes of the spirit.

devotions.title: Meditation And Success
devotions.html: Your success or prosperity is not the responsibility of God or anyone else; it is your responsibility depending on what you do with the word of God. Meditation is the key to seeing and doing what is needful for your success: “…that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” You cannot see how to do what is written if you do not take the time to meditate on it. During prayer there is a time to speak, a time to listen, and a time to meditate. This is where any believer can develop the inclination to be prophetic.

devotions.title: Meditation And The Prophetic
devotions.html: Note that becoming prophetic does not make you a prophet (as in the office of the prophet referred to in Ephesians 4:11). Every believer can be prophetic though not a prophet, and every prophet is prophetic. A prophetic person is one who, through adherence to meditation of the Word and prayer, has developed the ability to listen to the voice of God in his or her spirit, and is able to discern what God is showing him or saying to him regarding any particular aspect of his or her life, or the steps that need to be taken to continue in life. Abram's ability to obey God by leaving his country was due to his prophetic inclination (Genesis 12:1-4).

devotions.title: Meditation And Visions
devotions.html: A vision manifests as the ability to see in the spirit (Isaiah 6:1; Acts 2:17). The most basic form of a vision is a dream, and other forms are closed visions and open visions. The Bible does not teach us to ask for visions in our lives as that can be dangerous (2 Corinthians 11:14). The best way to move in these realms is by meditation of the Word and prayer, and your spirit will 'naturally' develop the supernatural ability to see in the spirit, whether through dreams, open or closed visions. Study Acts 9:10-18. All that is recorded there happened as a direct result of the men's inclination to prayer and meditation. God still desires to guide His people in this manner today.

devotions.title: Knowing The Voice
devotions.html: “I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now. Howbeit when He, the Spirit of truth, is come, He will guide you into all truth…” Safe to mention that Jesus was indicating that what is written in the Bible is not all that you need to live by. Although valuable for instruction and never to be undermined, it is in most cases general. However, the specific instruction must still be judged by the general instruction. By comparison it is like the specific Acts in Law having to work within the ambits of the Constitution. For example, the Bible does not tell you where to settle and build, or where to work, etc. You need the voice of the Spirit to guide you in those details.

devotions.title: Knowing The Voice (Part 2)
devotions.html: How was Abraham able to know that he needed to leave his country? (Genesis 12:1). Obviously he did not read it somewhere, but had to hear the voice of God speaking to him. The Father's desire, according to John 16:12-15 is for all His children to be led by the Spirit. But how will you be led if you do not know His voice? It takes diligence in prayer, the Word and meditation to learn to hear His voice that must guide you into the paths you must take for your life to the glory of God. If you do not strive to know and hear His voice you will spend all your life confined to the general instructions of the Word when you could go further through the Spirit.

secrets.title: About My Father's Business
secrets.teaching:
In Luke 2:49, Jesus asks His earthly parents – Mary and Joseph – a question: “How is it that you had to look for Me? Did you not see and know that it is necessary [as a duty] for Me to be in My Father's house and [occupied] about My Father's business?” (AMP).

From a tender age of twelve, Jesus had already caught on to the truth and vision that engaging with God should best be viewed and described as engaging in His business. This is what many of us believers have not yet realised… that God is a businessman. And businesspeople do not go about wasting time on activities that do not speak to the bottom line of the business. This means that whatever you do in the kingdom of God should be done with the mentality of business. No wonder most of the teachings of the Christ had to do with business. What does this have to do with prayer? Everything.

You see, you will lose the point until you start understanding the essence of prayer and guidance on how to conduct it as guided by the word. See a prayer session as a business meeting with God where you discuss serious business issues. Your prayer life will change as soon as you take up that mentality towards prayer. The primary purpose of a business meeting is not to make demands and address your wants. You attend a business meeting with a strategic mindset. It is where you discuss the what, the why, the how and the when of the progression of the business. And then when the business succeeds, everybody involved in it stands to benefit. Our problem has been that we have read wrongly into statements that the Lord Jesus made, like “I will do whatever you ask in my name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son. You may ask for anything in my name, and I will do it” (John 14:13-14, NIV). We have read these scriptures in isolation without caring to investigate the context in which they were spoken. And upon close examination we find that Jesus was talking about the kingdom of God and its advancement. In fact, these were His last and most important words about the kingdom, spoken during the Last Supper before He faced the cross of His crucifixion. Remember Matthew 6:33, “But seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well” (NIV).

We have thought that these statements were addressing our needs and earthly possessions and luxuries. Yet in line with Matthew 6:33 He was talking about things concerning the kingdom of God – that if it became first in our thinking and action, then all these things would be given to us. God knows that you need all those things in order to serve His kingdom effectively, so you do not have to waste time asking for things that He has already provided. Instead, occupy your prayer life with kingdom affairs. Continuing to talk about the business of the Father and its fruitfulness in John 15:1-2, Jesus identified the Father as the husbandman (or gardener, or vinedresser), and went on to say, “Greater love has no one than this: to lay down his life for one's friends” (John 15:13, NIV). This laying down of your life does not necessarily mean death, but setting aside your personal needs in prayer to pray for others and sacrificing your luxury for that of others. The highest form of prayer is the one offered on behalf of others. That was the kind of praying that Jesus spent His entire earthly life occupied in (Mark 1:35). “I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns also, because that is why I was sent” (Luke 4:43, NIV). That mission directed His prayer life. God's business has always been about restoring everything that the enemy stole from man in the Garden of Eden.

So what does 'restoring everything' mean in prayer? It means that you talk less and listen more. And if He sends you on an errand He will make sure that whatever you need for the mission is provided for (Philippians 4:19). If you need a car, a house, food and clothes, all those will be provided for without you having to focus on asking for them. But alas, we have missed the point and are caught up in non-essential desires, and we wonder when we do not see the answer to our prayers. Refer to James 4:1-3. Oh yes, He will give you the money, the houses, the cars and so forth, but the reason for all of that is not so you can be self-serving, but that you should be a blessing to other people. You are to use these provisions to minister salvation (healing, deliverance, and preservation) to other people (Genesis 12:2). And you should realise that to be the reason He deployed you in that neighbourhood and in that workplace. The primary reason that God will answer your prayer is so that you will meet the needs of the people around you, consistent with the objectives of His business (John 14:13). That is the most fulfilling life that you and I have been called to live on earth.

devotions.title: Prayer Is Business
devotions.html: In the mind of Christ, prayer is just as much a business activity as any other that needs your incomparable commitment. As a matter of fact He does not even see it as a religious activity; He never founded religion and has no concern for it. As a prayer warrior, you are a co-worker with God in the business of reconciling mankind back to Him. Prayer helps to prevent many deaths of the wicked, which God takes no pleasure in (Ezekiel 33:11). Standing in the gap and praying for the lost in this world is the foremost calling of every believer. It is not the responsibility of the evangelist and the preachers only, but for every man or woman that confesses Jesus as their Lord.

devotions.title: Beware Of Religion
devotions.html: Religious tendencies will cause you to operate at a level far below what God intends for you in prayer. Religious thoughts will kill your prayer life to where it becomes a drab and just another powerless religious exercise that has no life. If this describes your current situation then brace yourself for some positive change. “Is it possible to have a dialogue with God in prayer?” Most assuredly, yes! In fact, that is what prayer should be all about for you. Think of it as a telephone call with God instead of the traditional letter that would take fourteen days to come full circle. The religious mindset causes believers to be set back and settle for a boring time of prayer.

devotions.title: Accept The Challenge
devotions.html: Refuse to wallow in the swamps of religion when you can swim in the blessedness of a fulfilling fellowship with God. Jesus had face to face conversations with His disciples, and He said, “Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father” (John 14:9, NIV). If that is the case, then they were having conversations with the Father all along, and He responded to them in real time. Why should it be different now? We have allowed the veil of the flesh to get in the way of our spiritual being; otherwise it should not make any difference at all. Yes, it will not happen overnight, but it can be developed to get to that level if you commit to developing your walk and intimacy with the Lord.

devotions.title: Mind Of Christ
devotions.html: “For who has known the mind of the Lord so as to instruct Him? But we have the mind of Christ” (NIV). What does it mean to have the mind of Christ? It means that we have the mind that is influenced by the anointing of God (1 John 2:27). That was the mind that was active in our Lord Jesus by the same Spirit that now works in us. But that Spirit will not work in you if your mindset is not straightened out and renewed to the truth of God's word. In prayer, the Holy Spirit disseminates the thoughts of Christ into your mind so that you can think the way He does about any situation or matter that you pray about.

devotions.title: Think Like Jesus
devotions.html:
You can never be a fruitful believer if you do not approach prayer and whatever you do with the mindset of Jesus.

Thinking like Him automatically puts you in the position where you seek first His kingdom (Matthew 6:33). See the world and its population through the eyes of Jesus, and not through the eyes of the secular world. Thinking like Jesus will elevate any believer from being just a normal human being to being a powerful spiritual force that cannot be ignored in the spirit realm. Understand that the moment you enter the prayer closet, your spiritual presence is not limited to that little space, but that you can go farther than your body can go.

devotions.title: Think Like Jesus (Part 2)
devotions.html: “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the Lord” (Isaiah 55:8). Many believers quote this scripture out of context forgetting who it was addressing. It addressed the nation of Israel that was spiritually dead and could not relate with God spirit to spirit since Jesus had not yet gone to the cross to redeem any, hence He dealt with them on the basis of law. A born again believer can no longer run with such a narrative because He has given you His thoughts and shared His ways with you. “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus” (Philippians 2:5). “He is the head of the body, the church” (Colossians 1:18). Remember that the head and the body belong to the same person and share the same thoughts.

devotions.title: Sent Like Christ
devotions.html: “As you [Father] sent me into the world, I have sent them into the world.” You have the exact same mandate on you that was on Jesus Christ, except that you are not a substitute and sacrifice for anybody. However, in terms of all else that you read about Jesus doing in the Gospels, that is your assignment for as long as you are here on earth. Do not delight in only being the recipient of salvation, but delight more in that it has been given to you to give the same salvation to others as well. “Freely you have received; freely give” (Matthew 10:8, NIV).

devotions.title: Keep The Vision
devotions.html: Believers all over the world need to go back to the drawing board with God. The vision has been lost to some preachers, leading to a perpetration of a gospel of self-enrichment instead of bringing in the lost. “On hearing this, Jesus said to them, It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but those who are ill. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners” (Mark 2:17, NIV). Sinners are the number one concern of the Lord Jesus, who wants to see them coming into the sheepfold (John 10:16). He has called you and anointed you so that He can complete this job through you.

devotions.title: It Is Your Business
devotions.html: Humanity is your business whether you realise it or not. God is counting on you to come through for the lives of the lost around you. He is not even counting on the preachers that we so wrongly think He does. “So Christ Himself gave the apostles, the prophets, the evangelists, the pastors and teachers, [for what purpose?] to equip the people for works of service, so that the body of Christ may be built up” (Ephesians 4:11-12). The preachers equip you to take charge of the spiritual climate wherever you are and subdue every force of darkness, and thereby set the people of God free from bondage.

devotions.title: Not About You
devotions.html: Yes you are extremely precious to Jesus, but you must never lose sight of the reason He had you born again. Selfish believers who have lost sight of their salvation will take hours and days praying for themselves and their families. That may be good to do, but it must not land you on the wrong path for your salvation. Beside Jesus, men and women gave their lives to get this gospel to the people of the world that they never even knew existed. They understood the reason for their salvation and followed it through. “For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil” (1 John 3:8).

devotions.title: You Are A Soldier
devotions.html: The reason Holy Spirit is in you now is so that Jesus can be made manifest in you and continue to destroy the works of the enemy (1 John 3:8). You have been called to carry forward what He started, and that is the number one reason that you are alive today. He said, “Occupy till I come” (Luke 19:13). How do you occupy? By doing what He would be doing if He were in your place of work, neighbourhood, church, or whatever sphere of influence you occupy. You are there not to shine your own light, but to shine His light. All of this starts in prayer. Are you ready for this?

devotions.title: Born For Fruitfulness
devotions.html: “I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in Me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from Me you can do nothing” (John 15:5, NIV). Fruitfulness in scripture primarily refers to what you bring in to the kingdom of God. Here Jesus was giving a directive to the disciples about the way forward after His crucifixion, death and resurrection. It was, and still is about advancing the kingdom of God through vessels such as you. Restoring mankind to the original state that God had planned was what Jesus' coming was all about. He said, “Come, follow Me, and I will send you out to fish for people” (Matthew 4:19; 28:19-20).

devotions.title: Put Laziness Away
devotions.html: 'Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.” We would be very far, and so would God's kingdom be, if we approached our spiritual duties in the same way that we do our secular businesses. Business and laziness do not mix. Our secular occupations only have short-lived results, whilst our spiritual duties have eternal ramifications. How then can we be lacking in zeal for spiritual duties when we know that a lot hangs in the balance and many lives depend on how we align our spiritual engagement with God?

devotions.title: Making A Living?
devotions.html: We work with our hands in order to provide for our necessities (Acts 20:34); we engage spiritually in order to make an impact on the lives of others around us. We do not live to make a living. We give for a living, and live to make an impact. If your life is not about making an eternal difference to somebody else's life, then it is not worth living (John 15:13). Even your secular job should be geared towards changing someone else's life: “Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth” (Ephesians 4:28).

devotions.title: Your Greatest Debt
devotions.html: “I am a debtor both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish. That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome” (NIV). How many of us will leave this world with the unsettled debt of touching someone else's life? We owe it to Christ to extend the love that He extended to us to the rest of the world around us. Your neighbourhood should never become satan's paradise when you are there. All of hell should know that they cannot do as they please in your territory. You have been placed there to possess and control the spiritual climate in your community (Joshua 1:3). You can do that in your prayer closet.

devotions.title: Redeem The Time
devotions.html: “Be very careful, then, how you live – not as unwise, making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil. Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord's will is” (NIV). Do you know why our secular jobs hardly bring fulfilment? It is because they are not what we were designed for. You will never be fulfilled until your will is linked with His will so that you can do what He called you to do. You do not need a pulpit to do His will, you only need to listen to His direction as you spend time with Him in the secret place; He will show you how to make the most of every opportunity.

devotions.title: Sense Of Urgency
devotions.html: “As long as it is day, we must do the works of Him who sent Me. Night is coming, when no one can work” (NIV). Time on this planet is of great essence. We cannot afford to do things as though we will be here forever, and yet there is so much that we must accomplish in this short time. Jesus did His part in the 33 years – of which three were spent in active ministry – that He lived on earth. How much are we accomplishing in the time that we have? Are we chasing after His heartbeat or after our own temporary desires that have no eternal endurance? Every minute and every second in the prayer closet counts; is it so with you?

devotions.title: Sense Of Urgency (Part 2)
devotions.html: Prayer time is not for you to tick out the attendance register so you can feel better about yourself; it is where direction for the Father's business in your jurisdiction is discussed. “Very truly I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself; He can do only what He sees His Father doing…” (John 5:19, NIV). Jesus took the time to enquire from the Father what He needed to do, which was what brought results in His ministry. Many of us do not see results because we do not know how to enquire and know the Father's timetable for us. We must not put the resources of this world ahead of the Father's guidance to know what we must do.

devotions.title: Harvest Is Ripe
devotions.html: “Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? Behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest” (John 4:35). Jesus is showing us what He saved us here on earth to do. Your secular job is not your primary occupation, and neither does it address your destiny. You have been called into the Father's field, which is ready for harvest and waiting for you. The Father did not make you to keep another's vineyard (Song of Solomon 1:6), but His vineyard that He made you to co-owner with your Big Brother Jesus (Romans 8:17).

devotions.title: Spiritual Warfare
devotions.html: “Finally, be strong in the Lord and in His mighty power. Put on the full armour of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil's schemes. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms” (NIV). The truth is that all of hell fears what will happen when you enter that prayer closet with the knowledge of the mighty power that you possess, and that is the reason they do their best to see to it that you never find out. But now you know, and there is no excuse.
