secrets.title: Understanding The Blood Covenant
secrets.teaching:
Many believers are robbed of a fulfilling prayer life because of not knowing enough of what the covenant that was ratified in the blood of Jesus means for them. In fact, many do not fully understand that the entire word of God (or the Bible) is a documentation of the provisions of the covenants that God made with man all through the ages. In addition there seems to be limited understanding amongst some about what a covenant entails. Since this is a very broad subject, let us narrow it down for the purpose of what this journal is about. Whenever you go to pray, go there knowing that your prayer has already been answered in Jesus. Why? Because this last covenant, known as the New Testament, was made between God and the Man Jesus, who is the High Priest of our confession (Hebrews 3:1). Jesus has gone before God to present His own blood as a representative of all mankind (Hebrews 6:20). It is through this act that God sees us through the blood of Jesus, which is what makes that blood so powerful for our benefit.

What Are The Implications Of This Covenant?

From time immemorial, people understood covenant as a ritual involving two individuals who cut a covenant, mixing the bloods of the parties involved [in the wine]. These parties then drink of that wine, meaning that they drink of each other's blood in order to make them one. Some cultures still practise it even today. That is the reason the Lord Jesus always spoke of Him and the Father being one (John 17:21-22). If you consider the language used by Jesus in that prayer you will realise that He speaks as though He has already been crucified. That is the language of covenant, consistent with the language used in the case of Abraham having offered up Isaac as a sacrifice even though the latter was replaced by a ram (Genesis 22:12-13; Hebrews 11:17-19). This covenant made Jesus the possessor of heaven and earth as much as it did Abram (John 16:15; Genesis 14:18-20). Look closely at the blessing conferred upon Abram by Melchizedek, who was a type of Christ (Hebrews 7:3). If you do not pay close attention you will think that Melchizedek referred to God as the possessor of heaven and earth. But that is not what he did. He first blessed Abram and called him the possessor of heaven and earth (Genesis 14:19), and then he blessed God who delivered Abram's enemies into his hand (Genesis 14:20). How could he do that? As a prophet and high priest, he saw the covenant that God would make with Abram afterward, because he knew that no man could have done what Abram did if God was not with him.

The same is true about the Lord Jesus: His covenant with God made Him possessor of everything that belongs to the Father. But it does not end there: you need to understand the implications for you. Anyone who comes to Jesus becomes a joint-heir with Him of all that belongs to God (Romans 8:17). Our covenant with God through Jesus gives us access to everything that God has, and it also gives God access to everything that we have. We know that God is the Great Creator of everything, but what do we have that God could be so interested in? Unlike what religion would have us believe as fully unpacked in Prayer Secret 1, we have something very valuable to God, and something that He does not have. We have the physical bodies that God can use to relate with the lost humanity in this world. That is the reason Romans 12:1 urges us to offer our bodies as a living sacrifice to God. What it means is that we should allow God, by His Spirit, to indwell our bodies and live in us in order to do what He, without our bodies, cannot do on earth (1 Corinthians 6:19). Our bodies belong to Him just as much as His Spirit has been given to us, and we have access to His mighty power.

Therefore a clear understanding of this covenant helps to anchor our minds on the unchangeable nature of the promises of God to us (Hebrews 6:19). You enter the presence of God in prayer with the full knowledge that all His promises are 'Yes' and 'Amen' in Christ to the glory of God (2 Corinthians 1:20). You understand the nature of the partnership that you have with God for the advancement of His kingdom, which has now become your kingdom as well. You are not only a servant, but also a joint-heir with Christ of the kingdom which God has prepared for us. Therefore you should take the time to dig deeper into what this covenant means for you and God, as well as in relation to all of creation. This ownership mentality will change your attitude toward prayer, as well as how you actually pray.

devotions.title: A Better Covenant
devotions.html: “But in fact the ministry [that] Jesus has received is as superior to theirs as the covenant of which He is mediator is superior to the old one, since the new covenant is established on better promises” (NIV). Based on the pure, spotless blood of the Lamb of God that gives new life to all that receive it, a much better platform has been provided for us to have communion with the Godhead. It is better than everything that we read about in the Old Testament. Our prayer lives should therefore yield greater results than what those of the Old Testament saints did.

devotions.title: The Blood Transfusion
devotions.html: “For the life of the flesh is in the blood… for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” The blood that you received from Jesus has given you new life that is free from all condemnation and guilt. This transfusion took place during the new birth; hence “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creation: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new” (2 Corinthians 5:17). Failure to understand this will greatly hamper your prayer life. You commune with God as a new creature, whose blood is as pure as that of Jesus because it comes from Him.

devotions.title: Power Of Covenant
devotions.html: Your covenant with God places you in a position to harvest the strength (or power) of God and enables you to do what you have no power to do on your own. [It is the same principle by which a wife benefits from her husband's name]. The blood of Jesus in you authorises you to accomplish what you would not have the right to accomplish on your own and without that blood. That is the confidence that you have in prayer through Christ. His name is the signature on the promissory note; use it.

devotions.title: Your Covenant Obligation
devotions.html: “Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God – this is your true and proper worship” (NIV). Everything else that you do will not carry weight until you give your body to God as a living sacrifice. That is the only thing that you can offer God and it adds value to Him because He does not have one of His own that He can use on this earth. No matter how weak you think it is, hand it over to Him, and He will make it strong.

devotions.title: Your Covenant Obligation (Part 2)
devotions.html: Note that He asked for your body just as it is (“voetstoots”), and He will refurbish it for His own use. That is the only reasonable act of service that He asks of you when you compare it with all that you stand to benefit from the relationship with Him. How do you do that? “Never be lacking in zeal, but keep your spiritual fervour, serving the Lord” (Romans 12:11, NIV). Learn to not listen to the dictates of your body, but rather let it follow the desires of the Spirit. You will banish laziness to study the Word, pray and meditate in fellowship with God. It is through these that we obey God and accomplish His will.

devotions.title: Drink His Blood
devotions.html: “He that eateth My flesh, and drinketh My blood, dwelleth in Me, and I in him.” Have you noticed that the blood of Jesus is the only blood that mankind is permitted to drink? (Leviticus 17:14). His blood represents everything that He is – His life, love, health, character, peace, and all of His other attributes. It is through your full association with His blood that your weaknesses are undermined and you put on His strength and dominion over the works of the flesh. It will also change your language for the better, which greatly impacts your prayer life.

devotions.title: Drink His Blood (Part 2)
devotions.html: “He that eateth My flesh, and drinketh My blood, dwelleth in Me, and I in him” (John 6:56). What does that mean? It means the merging that takes place between you and Jesus. The only closest example to illustrate this is the union that takes place between a husband and wife in marriage. They benefit from the strengths of each other. And when you approach the Father in prayer, it is just like Jesus Himself doing it, which is why you must do it in His name.

devotions.title: Keep Yourself Reminded
devotions.html: “After the same manner also He took the cup, when He had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in My blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of Me.” Mankind has the tendency to forget. The ritual of the Holy Communion serves as a prophetic action to remind us of the covenant that He has ratified for our benefit. It is not just to remember Him, but also what he has done in you, and what He has made you to be through His blood.

devotions.title: Keep Yourself Reminded (Part 2)
devotions.html: “For those who eat and drink without discerning the body of Christ eat and drink judgment on themselves” (1 Corinthians 11:29, NIV). The breaking of the bread symbolises the body of Jesus that was broken for us. Furthermore, it reminds you about the value of the other believers who make up the body of Christ, who have also eaten of His flesh and have drunk of His blood, and have thus also become one with you. Harming them is harming yourself, which is “why many among you are weak and ill, and a number of you have fallen asleep” (or have died) (verse 30).

devotions.title: The Kingdom Is Yours
devotions.html: “Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom.” We are accustomed to saying, “For Yours is the kingdom, the power and the glory,” which is forever true. But He has said that it is His good pleasure (or it pleases Him perfectly) to give you that kingdom. When excited, kings of this world will promise their loved ones great things up to the half of their kingdoms (Esther 5:6; Mark 6:22-23), but your Father in heaven does not give in halves – He has given you the kingdom. Renew your mind to this truth and see how it impacts your prayer life.

devotions.title: Right Of Access
devotions.html: “Therefore, brothers and sisters, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, by a new and living way opened for us through the curtain, that is, His body…” Note that the general assembly of the nation of Israel was not allowed into the Most Holy Place, but was open only to the high priest after the necessary washings to cleanse him from impurities. Contravening that would result in the death of the offender. But the blood of Jesus has made it possible for us today to enter the very presence of the Holy God.

devotions.title: The Life Of God
devotions.html: God's life has been infused into you through the blood of Christ. This life makes you one with the Father just as it made Jesus one with the Father. Stepping into your prayer closet is stepping into the place where you can claim your inheritance. You do not pray in order to try and please or impress God; you pray in order to see to it that the job that He has set aside for you to do gets done.

devotions.title: No Longer Alien
devotions.html: “Consequently, you are no longer foreigners and strangers, but fellow citizens with God's people and also members of His household” (NIV). The blood of Jesus has ensured this to be the case with you – you are His blood-brother or blood-sister. Stop thinking any less of yourself than what God has said in His word. You have as much right to 'play' on your Father's lap like any beloved child does, and He is ever ready to listen to your requests and grant them to you in real time.

devotions.title: Do Not Fear
devotions.html: The blood of Christ at work in your life has 'disabled' fear in your life – the cancer that corrupts the prayers of many believers so that they go unanswered. This blood has rendered you indestructible, so that even if they kill your body, it will rise again. They cannot inflict death on the blood that has sanctified you because it has defeated death through its characteristic of being full of life and devoid of death. So you do not work from a standpoint of death or darkness, but from a standpoint of life and light.

devotions.title: Enter With Boldness
devotions.html: “Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.” This world would be a much better place if the body of Christ understood and believed what the blood of Christ has accomplished for humanity. Every droplet of His blood was worth the work that He accomplished. The believer should take full advantage of this blood to manifest God to the lost world and recover for God what the devil has stolen from mankind.

devotions.title: Enter With Boldness (Part 2)
devotions.html: There is nothing that prevents you from approaching the Creator of the universe – your own heavenly Father. Do not fear to own Him; He also owns you according to the covenant right that He has with you. He will never walk away from covenant. “I will not violate My covenant or alter what My lips have uttered” (Psalm 89:34, NIV). That is the kind of God that you serve and pray to. You can go into His presence knowing that what He has promised is already done.

devotions.title: His Holy Armour
devotions.html: “Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” Notice that you do not put on your armour, but the armour of God Himself. When you have that armour on, the devil cannot tell the difference between you and God. He recognises that armour and he remembers that it is what whipped him and took away the keys of death, hell and the grave a while before Christ was raised from the dead. Put it on even in prayer, and your victory is guaranteed.

devotions.title: His Holy Armour (Part 2)
devotions.html: Do not be bothered that at first the armour of God might not fit you snugly. Wear it anyway, and you will grow in it. Do not do these battles with the armour of the flesh. What is the armour of God? It is Truth, Righteousness, Peace, Faith, Salvation, the Word of God, and Prayer. If you take a close look at these, they are all products of the Word of God, which is Jesus – the Word made flesh – working in you. His word is therefore the most powerful weapon in the universe. Jesus used it when He said to satan, “It is written…” (Matthew 4:4, 7, 10).

devotions.title: Stop The Whining
devotions.html: After all, and in view of all that the blood of Jesus has accomplished for you, don't you ever get caught going to God on the basis of who you are, what you can or cannot do. Go to God on the basis of what Christ, through His blood, has accomplished for you. Receive your forgiveness through His blood and understand that His blood gives you a place fit for the perfect Jesus before God.

devotions.title: Stop The Whining (Part 2)
devotions.html: Stop calling yourself a worm and worthless being when you go to God in prayer (Psalm 22:6). That is a great insult to Him because then you are insinuating that Jesus is also a worm (because you are a joint-heir with Him). God is not in covenant with worms. Worms have not been made in the image of God and in His likeness. God's concern through the ages has been mankind, not lions, elephants, or any other animals, and certainly not worms. He is your Father, and you look exactly like Him (John 1:12).

secrets.title: Fasting And Spiritual Warfare
secrets.teaching:
It is human tendency to want to resort to some form of enforcement when things do not seem to work according to plan. People have Plan B, Plan C, and so forth for almost anything. Even in prayer, people tend to want to resort to fasting when it seems that there is a delay in the answer coming forth. However, gears are changed carelessly when we begin to think that it is the fasting that brings answers to prayer because then you tend to misplace your faith on fasting rather than on God. Yet that is not what the word of God teaches about fasting. Fasting is a very good practice, but it has its place in the life of a believer. If you examine scriptures that talk about fasting and praying you will find that one is not meant to reinforce the other. For example, Jesus says nothing about fasting in His teaching about faith and prayer in Mark 11:22-24. He talks about praying and believing in one's heart, and does not refer to fasting. Yet He also teaches about fasting, but with the knowledge that the people already had background understanding about the subject. “When you fast, do not look somber as the hypocrites do, for they disfigure their faces to show others they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full. But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face, so that it will not be obvious to others that you are fasting, but only to your Father, who is unseen; and your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you” (Matthew 6:16-18, NIV). Notice that He is not introducing the subject of fasting to them, but how to do it and what to do when they fast.

Believers tend to think that God hears them better, or sees how serious they are when they fast. Yet fasting is not meant for that at all. It is not meant to twist the arm of God into doing what He will not do, neither is it meant to demonstrate to God just how serious one is. It is not even meant to speed up answers to prayer. We receive answers to prayer by faith in His promises. Nowhere in the Bible is fasting responsible for answers to prayer. So why should you fast? Fasting changes you; it does not change or move God in any way. It helps to place you in a position where you can easily receive from God, but it is not a replacement for faith. You can fast all you want, but if you do not have faith you will not receive because the connection is broken.

Jesus was teaching that fasting is a private spiritual affair. This means that it works more like reconditioning a product in order for it to work well. When you fast you actually feed your spirit, thus putting your spirit being first (in a sense), and subduing the body (1 Corinthians 9:27; Colossians 3:5). You do not fast without taking some quality time on the word of God and prayer, otherwise all you would be doing is just going hungry for a couple of days. In other words, fasting without focusing on your spiritual development is no different from engaging in a diet program. Also, it will serve you well to announce your fasting to God before you start, thus clearly setting the parameters of your fast to keep you in line. So what happens when you fast? You develop your spirit to become fit, more sensitive to the Holy Spirit, and easily apt to following the leading of the Spirit. Fasting does to your spirit what a concentrated exercise program will do to an athlete's body when he is preparing to compete in the Olympic Games. You become more spiritually agile, sharp, and strong enough to handle tricky situations. That was the reason Jesus embarked on a fast before He started with His public ministry (Matthew 4:1-2).

The Prophet Isaiah spoke about fasting as the Spirit of the Lord inspired him in Isaiah 58:1-14. You will do good to read that for yourself. There you will notice that he shows them the wrong way and the correct way of fasting, as well as the results that they would experience during and after a fast. You will also do well to understand that when you fast, you should also do it in faith, which is why you must stay on the word of God and prayer when you do. Fasting is also a broad subject for which we do not have time or space to explore in all detail, but the little that we have shared should give you a head start in at least doing it the correct way.

devotions.title: According To The Word
devotions.html: If you want to be safe, do whatever you do according to the guidelines provided in the word of God, and not just because it is a ritual that people engage in. Seek the knowledge and understanding of the subject before you embark on it. In that manner you will avoid gravitating into error and religion. Did you know that religious people also fast? Yes, satanists, witchdoctors and witches also engage in fasting for their own reasons. The word of God will teach you how to fast according to His will.

devotions.title: In Fastings Often
devotions.html: “In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.” Whilst fasting can help to keep your body in good shape physically through the benefits that are associated with it, it helps to do it correctly, especially when you do it often. There is a thin line between fasting and a diet program. As you may be aware, there are different types of fasting, from fasting certain foods to just taking certain liquids to a completely dry fast. It is always advisable to know how to do it as doing it foolishly may end up doing more harm than good.

devotions.title: It Changes You
devotions.html: Nothing around you or outside of you changes as a result of your fasting. The fasting changes your spirit being, and consequently you influence your environment and surroundings. As a result, somebody stepping into your 'personal space' or coming into close proximity with you may sense the energy, or what others may refer to as 'aura', or the anointing. That is what is inside you coming out and influences your surroundings. In scripture it is referred to in terms such as 'the shadow of Peter' (Acts 5:15) and 'virtue' or 'power' (Mark 5:30).

devotions.title: It Changes You (Part 2)
devotions.html: Your fasting will not change other people, but it will put you in a position to bring the change to others as you minister to them under the anointing. It helps you to loosen the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, to let the oppressed go free, and to break or destroy every yoke (Isaiah 58:6; 10:27). That was what the anointing on Jesus did, and the same happened through His apostles afterward as narrated in the Acts of the Apostles.

devotions.title: Seeking the Lord
devotions.html: Fasting comes in handy when you take it upon yourself to seek the Lord. You can decide to enter into any particular type of fasting for a predetermined period as you seek the Lord. Of course He is not far from you, but you may find that your spiritual senses have gone blunt for whatever reason, and you have become spiritually dense (Hebrews 5:11). Then fasting, study of the Word, prayer and meditation will help restore your spiritual sensitivity, which is so needful in your walk with God.

devotions.title: No Budget Beater
devotions.html: Fasting is not a method of managing your budget. In fact, it is more effective to fast while you give away the meals that you would have had if you had not been fasting. This becomes a more effective tool of evangelism. Fasting to beat your budget is simply a diet program which will not count spiritually. You cannot cut corners; otherwise everyone facing starvation would be a spiritual giant as they go into involuntary fasting. Your motive counts and it matters.

devotions.title: Praying At Midnight
devotions.html: Is praying at midnight the best time to pray? Some people believe so, and say that it is because forces of darkness are more active then. However, scripture does not endorse that thinking. Forces of darkness are active at any time of day or night, which is why all sorts of atrocities are committed around the clock. If you feel comfortable praying at midnight, it is fine; however, it should not be because witches and other forces are at work then. In fact, you may find yourself praying in response to fear, which renders your prayer void. “It is vain for thee to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so He giveth His beloved sleep” (Psalm 127:2).

devotions.title: Praying At Midnight (Part 2)
devotions.html: Why did Paul and Silas pray and sing praises to God at midnight? The Bible does not say, but surely they were not establishing a prayer time pattern; it may have been the time that seemed best for them under the circumstances (Acts 16:25). But Jesus would rise up early before dawn and go to a solitary place to pray (Mark 1:35). Sometimes He would go out and spend the night in prayer (Luke 6:12), and other times He would go out to pray before and into the evening (Matthew 14:23). So you can see just how at the peak of revival the time of prayer did not make any difference.

devotions.title: Praying At Midnight (Part 3)
devotions.html: Of course, there is an advantage to praying at night. In most cases it is quiet and there are very few or no disturbances. Undisturbed prayer time is often great and fruitful. Do not stay awake because of fear of the activities in darkness. “You will not fear the terror of night” (Psalm 91:5). It does not matter if all of hell marches toward you at night; you are safe if you dwell in the secret place of the Most High (Psalm 91:1). You already have the promise that sends you to sleep with confidence. “When you lie down, you will not be afraid… your sleep will be sweet” (Proverbs 3:24, NIV).

devotions.title: Sleep Is Healthy
devotions.html: Did you know that your spirit never goes to sleep even when your body is resting in sleep? Your spirit – the real you – is like God who never sleeps nor slumbers (Psalm 121:3-4). It is always alert, so that even when forces of darkness try to attack you while your body is resting, your spirit will most definitely deal with them if the need arises; otherwise you have the angels of God keeping guard over you, which is a great reinforcement against evil. Give your body enough sleep, which is healthy for you, and you will become more useful in the earth as you live longer.

devotions.title: Picking Battles Wisely
devotions.html: There are believers who think war at all times. Whereas we are in a war, not everything is war. Many of the prayers that some believers who lack understanding make are not even scriptural, and are therefore never backed by Heaven. For example, “Any spirit that is assigned against my…, catch fire and die in Jesus' name!” Beloved, spirits never die, but are eternal. That decree is therefore invalid and a waste of breath. Nowhere in the Scriptures does Jesus or any of His apostles kill demons or spirits. They can be subdued and arrested (Psalm 149:6-9; Mark 5:8; Luke 11:24-26; Revelation 20:10 & 21:14-15), but not killed.

devotions.title: The Mighty Warrior
devotions.html: Spiritual warfare does not mean you go around casting out every demon in the way. That can be very exhausting. It means though, that you have put on the armour of God in order to be able to withstand the devil's wiles as and when occasion arises (Ephesians 6:13). Take note: “so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground” (NIV). It is vain to try and engage in warfare without the whole armour of God; in fact, that results in many casualties and prisoners of war.

devotions.title: The Mighty Warrior (Part 2)
devotions.html: 2 Timothy 2:24-26, “And the servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome but must be kind to everyone, able to teach, not resentful. Opponents must be gently instructed, in the hope that God will grant them repentance leading them to a knowledge of the truth, and that they will come to their senses and escape from the trap of the devil, who has taken them captive to do his will” (NIV). These are prisoners of war taken captive by the devil as a result of strife in their lives. That can happen to any believer who entertains strife in their life.

devotions.title: Banish The Strife
devotions.html: Any form of strife is deadly to a believer. You get involved in that strife, and you set yourself for any spiritual warfare, you have just made yourself vulnerable to attack. The enemy will just pull the rug from under you, and all the ammunition that you have will be neutralised by the strife in your life (whether in church, at home, in your marriage, or anywhere else), and the enemy will imprison you. It is not a suggestion: “…the servant of the Lord must not be quarrelsome.” If you want to engage in spiritual warfare, get rid of strife and keep it out of your life for good.

devotions.title: God Hates Discord
devotions.html: “There are six things the Lord hates, seven that are detestable to him… a false witness who pours out lies and a person who stirs up conflict in the community” (NIV). The KJV says, “…and he that soweth discord among brethren.” Why does God hate strife? It is characteristic of the devil who engaged a third of the angels in it, and were thrown out of heaven as a result. That is the same trick that he uses to neutralise a believer and renders them useless in battle. How do you control strife? Learn to tame your tongue.

devotions.title: Tame Your Tongue
devotions.html: “But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.” Whilst it is true that no man can tame the tongue, there is one thing that can, and that is the word of God. That is what you find if you read further down the chapter. It refers to the wisdom that descends from above and contrasts it with the wisdom of the world. The wisdom from above that tames the tongue is the word of God. You must strive to be a man or woman that is full of the Word in order to be a good soldier of Jesus Christ (2 Timothy 2:3-4).

devotions.title: The Writer’s Pen
devotions.html: “My heart is stirred by a noble theme as I recite my verses for the king; my tongue is the pen of a skillful writer” (NIV). When your tongue is tamed, it becomes the pen that writes skillfully in the spirit, writing the vision that the Lord shows you in prayer (Habakkuk 2:2-3). The vision becomes the decree that you make in the spirit, which shall be established and brought to pass (Job 22:28). Let your heart that is filled with the word of God that will instruct your tongue what to write in the spirit, and an answer to your prayer is guaranteed.

devotions.title: What About Patience?
devotions.html: “For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.” Praying for the lost, communities and nations, and standing in the gap to see change taking place requires patience. You fast and pray, and in the spirit subdue the powers that control nations from the air. Change takes place in the air before it manifests in the physical world. What you say with your mouth in the interim is crucial: it will either enforce the decrees made, or it will revoke what has been decreed so that change will not manifest.

devotions.title: Zeal Of God
devotions.html: “To those who sold doves He said, 'Get these out of here! Stop turning my Father's house into a market!' His disciples remembered that it is written: 'Zeal for your house will consume me'” (NIV). What consumes you? Jesus was consumed (or eaten up) with the zeal of His Father's house. The house of the Lord and His work was what He was passionate about. Zeal will wake you up when others are asleep so that you can pray without having to drag your feet to the prayer closet. Zeal will drive you to the Word so that the sword of the Spirit will always be ready in your mouth to execute vengeance upon the enemy (Psalm 149:6-9).

devotions.title: Zeal Of God (Part 2)
devotions.html: Let the word of God cultivate the zeal of God in your life so that you can be a prayer warrior that is worth your salt. There are levels of spiritual navigation that you simply will not venture into without the passion that is needed. “I am a foreigner to my own family, a stranger to my own mother's children; for zeal for your house consumes me, and the insults of those who insult you fall on me” (Psalm 69:8-9). That describes Jesus so perfectly (Mark 3:21; John 7:5). Your own people may not understand you when you start tapping into these levels, but the Lord will.

secrets.summary: Fasting changes you, not God. Learn its true place alongside faith, and how to fight wisely in spiritual warfare.

salvation:
God loves you – no matter who you are or what your past was like. He gave His one and only Son Jesus for you. The Bible tells us, “…whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life” (John 3:16). Jesus, driven by love, laid down His life for mankind. He died, was buried and rose from the grave, so that we could spend eternity with Him in heaven and experience His best while we are living on the earth. If you would like to receive Jesus into your life, say the following prayer aloud and mean it from your heart:

Heavenly Father, I come to You admitting that I am a sinner. Right now, I choose to turn away from sin, and I ask You to cleanse me of all unrighteousness. I believe that Your Son, Jesus, died on the cross to take away my sins. I also believe that He rose from the dead so that I might be forgiven of my sins and be made righteous through faith in Him. I call on the name of Jesus Christ to be the Saviour and Lord of my life. Jesus, I choose to follow You and ask that You fill me with the power of the Holy Spirit. I declare that I am free from sin and am full of the righteousness of God. I am saved in Jesus' name. Amen.

If you prayed this prayer to receive Jesus Christ as your Saviour for the first time, and even if you were a backslider who decided to come back to God, please contact us on the following details so that we can help you further: letschat@timelesswisdom.co.za with the subject - Prayer of Salvation.
